MAJOR: Recommendation is recovered by regex-scraping the rendered human table (`_parse_recommendation` over subprocess stdout). This re-encodes the gate renderer's format in the trail module, contradicting the "one evidence reader" invariant the doc claims; any wording change in `architect_review.py` silently yields "recommendation unavailable". Read the structured `engineering/reviews/<ID>-<sha>.json` instead.

Every `show` now spawns two subprocess gate renders (design + diff) with no cache; render latency is now coupled to gate tooling and, on timeout/exception, the trail silently degrades to "(cannot render)". Coupling a read-only projection to live subprocess execution is a scalability and availability risk for a frequently-run command.

Re-run/audit history is no longer rendered: the old per-event table (seq, per-run status/duration/summary) is replaced by latest-per-stage plus a `Runs` count. Observability/auditability regression — the trail store is append-only but `show` no longer surfaces the history it was created to expose (docs only assert it "remains in events()").

`current_stage` marks any stage with fail/error/blocked as "blocked at <stage>", including post-merge stages (pr/merge/delivery/completion) — contradicting the documented rule ("a committed pre-merge gate") and mislabelling completed-then-failed post-merge steps as blocking.
MINOR: Timeout silently reduced 60s→20s with no rationale; combined with the new subprocess-per-show design this is a truncation risk on large review evidence.

Status vocabulary literals ("reviewed (recommendation unavailable)", "APPROVE WITH ATTENTION", CLOSED_STATUSES) are duplicated across `execution_trail.py`, the lifecycle doc, and tests with no shared constants — drift will break the documented invariants.
Failures are `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` from a library function; no structured logging/counter, so render degradation is unobservable in automation.
`current_stage` is emitted twice (header and §3) and again in the final table; inconsistent rendering surface for one value.
Tests patch `_review_evidence` in the ordering test, so the recommendation-display path for Gate 2.5 (diff) and the `Runs` re-run count are never asserted end-to-end.

`_parse_recommendation`'s greedy `[A-Z][A-Z0-9 _/-]*` will swallow trailing qualifier words (e.g. "APPROVE PENDING 2 FINDINGS") into the "recommendation", silently expanding the accepted status set beyond the three documented values.
NIT: `id-blocks.json` bumps `reserved_up_to` to 1484 and adds two sessions (1483, 1484); reservation for an unrelated session ID rides along in this item's diff — verify both are actually claimed.
`_flow_rows` and `_box` iterate dict keys by index rather than `.items()`; readable but fragile under future key reordering.
`current_stage` derives "complete" from a status string alone even when required stages are missing — a stale/wrong status yields a false "complete" in the final table.
SUMMARY: Solid acceptance-criteria coverage (section order, current-stage, dedupe, disposition key, empty/partial items) and good doc/test pairing, but the architecture moved the wrong way: a read-only projection now shells out twice per render and recovers structured state by regex-scraping a human table, while per-event audit history was dropped from the output. Fix the evidence-reading path (structured JSON, cached) and restore or explicitly surface re-run history before shipping; also reconcile `current_stage` with the documented pre-merge-only blocking rule.
